Not the cheapest, but fresh and reliable seafood restaurant.
Mar 2026 • Friends
In District 1 and near numerous serviced apartments including ours, so we opted to arrange for takeaway instead of dining in because: 
1) Though it was sheltered, it was still an open-air shop by the busy road. They might have air-conditioned seating upstairs but not sure if that area's open.
2) Rowdy beer guzzlers made it hard to enjoy a proper meal.

Service: 
Staff in this branch (maybe their most popular outlet since it's in town) spoke English so tourists could order easily.

Prices:
Straightforward transparent - we chose our seafood and paid by weight, chose our preferred method of cooking and paid a fixed "cooking fee" of ~10usd.

Tastes:
Undeniably fresh, and their salted egg and garlic styles were very tasty! Free condiments such as peanuts, rice crisps, cucumber slices and various spicy and sour sauces made the dishes even more appetizing. Non-seafood dishes like fried rice and stir-fried morning glory were good too!

A 20-minute wait for all five dishes, and with the nicely packed aluminum-trays, it was easy to just lay them out on the dining table and enjoy 'em in the comfort of our serviced apartment!

Over-priced seafood restaurant with sub-pat service
Mar 2026 • Couples
Incredibly overpriced seafood restaurant. Our bill came out to $95/person - equivalent to what we would have paid in the US. The food, when it finally came, was good but overpriced. We have traveled all over Vietnam and this was our only disappointing dining experience. And given we were paying around $600, I found it offensive that our server counted the napkins at the end of the meal and charged us for those we used - oh, and charged us for the mochis she brought us at the end of the meal which we did not ask for and which she said were free. Juat left us with an icky feeling - would recommend people avoid.
